claims.text: Tailored alloying and processing can produce serrated or refined interfacial microstructures in high-entropy-alloy coatings.
High-entropy-alloy multilayer coatings with serrated or refined interfaces resist time-dependent plastic deformation better than coatings without those interfaces.
The improved resistance results from inhibition of dislocation accumulation.
Serrated interfaces promote a more uniform distribution of strain.
Conventionally prepared multilayer high-entropy-alloy coatings with homogenized interfaces exhibit creep under sustained loading.
Adjusting sputtering, annealing, or bias voltage can induce serrated or refined interfaces in a multilayer coating.
Adding selected alloying elements can promote interfacial or grain refinement in high-entropy-alloy coatings.
Serrated and refined multilayer interfaces act as barriers to dislocation motion.
The modified interfaces restrict dislocation migration and pile-up through geometric barriers.
More uniform strain distribution reduces local strain concentration.
Restricting dislocation motion and redistributing strain reduce creep rate and time-dependent plastic deformation.
Under identical testing conditions, the engineered coating will accumulate creep strain more slowly than a homogeneous, non-engineered coating.
Under identical testing conditions, the engineered coating will exhibit less total time-dependent plastic deformation than the homogeneous control.
The proposed behavior applies in temperature and load regimes dominated by dislocation-mediated plasticity.
The proposed benefit may not persist at very high temperatures or extreme loads where diffusion or other failure mechanisms dominate.
The magnitude of creep-resistance improvement depends on alloy composition and processing parameters.

contradictions.description: The initial state describes the comparator as a multilayer coating with conventional homogenized interfaces, whereas the baseline and experiment describe a homogeneous coating. This leaves it unclear whether the controlled difference is interface morphology alone or multilayer architecture as well.
